h: Cranford, Sand Carpets and a Giant Telescope
p: Knutsford has a literary claim to fame. The novelist Elizabeth Gaskell grew up here, and the town was the model for Cranford, her gentle tale of small-town life. Wander King Street and you'll find plenty of independent shops, old coaching inns and cosy places to eat, with the Gaskell Memorial Tower an eye-catching Italianate building in the middle of town.

The town has a quirky tradition too. On special occasions, including the Royal May Day celebrations, people decorate the pavements with patterns of coloured sand, a custom known as sanding that is said to go back centuries.

For a brilliant second stop, Jodrell Bank, a short drive south near Holmes Chapel, is home to the giant Lovell Telescope, one of the largest steerable radio telescopes in the world and part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The visitor centre explains how scientists listen to the universe, and seeing the dish tower over the Cheshire fields is something else.
Tatton Park is the big neighbour on Knutsford's doorstep, but don't overlook the smaller country houses around here, such as Arley Hall with its famous gardens.

At the bird park, bring a hat or hood: birds of prey fly low and fast, and a light shower won't stop a display. Keep little ones close and quiet when the birds are on the glove, and you'll get much better views.
